I wanted dice that feel like dice. You click roll, they tumble across the table, bump into each other, and land on the number you actually rolled, on everyone's screen at the same time. That's Dicer. It's a lighter take on what Dice So Nice does, built for Foundry v14, and it stays out of the way: when no dice are rolling, it isn't doing anything at all.

Make them yours

Open the theme browser and you'll find more than twenty sets to start from. Then open the dice editor and make something of your own: clear resin with fire or a storm swirling inside, metal, marble, pearl, wood, a polished gem. Pick your own font, put your group's logo on the 20, wrap a picture around the die. You can give each character their own dice, roll attacks in one set and damage in another, or keep it simple and use one set for everything. If you already have Dice So Nice dice sets from other modules, they show up too, 3D models and all.

Damage you can see

A fireball should look like a fireball. In Pathfinder 2e, Starfinder 2e and D&D 5e, damage dice come in their element on their own: fire dice glow and leave embers behind them, cold dice frost over, lightning crackles, acid drips. Roll a natural 20 on one and it goes off. In any other system, add a tag like 2d6[fire] and you get the same thing.

The big moments

Natural 20s get a celebration, and natural 1s get the suitably sad moment they deserve. If you have JB2A, you can use its animations too. GMs and players can set their own rules: play a sound when someone crits, run a macro on a 1, light up a die when it hits a certain number. And a roll you're not meant to see stays secret. No peeking at the GM's dice.

Meet your dice pet

My favourite part. Pick a little mimic, slime or dragonling, give it your colour, and it hangs around the table watching your rolls. It cheers when a friend rolls a 20 and sulks after you roll badly a few times in a row. It coughs when a fire die lands next to it and shivers at frost, and every damage type gets its own reaction. Its eyes follow your cursor. Click it and it purrs; click it too much and it gets grumpy, turns its back on you and hops off for a bit. Drag it anywhere you like and that's where it'll wait. And yes, if a d20 hits it hard enough, it goes splat.

A dice tray that knows your game

There's a little tray under the chat box. Click a few dice, add a modifier, and roll. It knows your system: advantage and disadvantage in 5e, fortune and misfortune and one-click DC 5 and DC 11 flat checks in Pathfinder and Starfinder, Duality rolls in Daggerheart, edges and banes in Draw Steel.

And a few more things

You can throw dice by hand, then pick up the ones that landed and fling them around while you wait for your turn. GMs can give each player their own spot on the screen to roll in. Anyone can tell Dicer to skip the rolls they don't care about, like initiative or huge fistfuls of dice. If you use Pixels or other electronic dice, Dicer works with those too.

Modules and systems that talk to Dice So Nice keep working with Dicer. Just turn Dice So Nice off in the worlds where you use Dicer.

Questions, ideas or bugs: everything is on the wiki, and you can open an issue anytime. Have fun rolling!
